newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hostages freed after S.Korean police storm bus.
newsitem.headline: Hostages freed after S.Korean police storm bus.

text.p: South Korean police stormed a bus in Seoul on Thursday to free 34 passengers held hostage for more than an hour by a knife-wielding man, witnesses said.

A dozen police wearing bullet-proof vests and armed with automatic rifles kicked open the bus door and fired teargas before rushing in and seizing the man, identified as Kwon Shin-hong, 55. They bundled him into a waiting police van.
The bus driver was injured but no passengers, who included eight children, appeared to be hurt in the raid.
Freed hostages said the man appeared to be mentally unstable and had been carrying what he claimed was a home-made bomb.
They said Kwon took over the bus around 2:30 p.m. (0530 GMT) and ordered the driver to go to the Presidential Blue House after complaining the country was "full of communists".
The driver refused, and instead drove the bus to a government complex in central Seoul.
"The man was sitting near the front of the bus when he suddenly got up and tossed a bundle in a plastic bag under the driver's seat," said passenger Park Young-shik, 40.
"He said it was TNT and he would blow up the bus if he wasn't taken to the Blue House. Then he stood blocking the door, holding a 15cm knife."
During the stand-off, which occurred as authorities elsewhere in this capital moved to crack down on continuing labour strife, the hostages huddled at the rear of the bus.
Some of the children peered out the windows at police marksmen crouched around the back of vehicle.
Most passengers, while red-faced and breathing with some difficulty from the teargas, appeared unperturbed by the ordeal.
Some children only broke into tears when scores of reporters and cameramen surged around them.
